# Christopher Wood (Jefferies) on "Conversation with Kushal" — Research Note

**Source:** YouTube transcript `YOUTUBE118LODHA389.txt` (auto-generated, ~76 min). Host: Kushal Lodha. Guest: Christopher Wood, Global Head of Equity Strategy, Jefferies (*Greed & Fear*).
**Approx. date:** around Aug–Sep 2026. This is inferred from the content: a recent 25 bp Fed hike, the US 10Y "just touched 5%", Greed & Fear's 30th anniversary "end of July", and Bitcoin "peaked in October". It is not stated explicitly.
**Labels:** [FACT] = verifiable data point he cites (not yet verified by us) · [VIEW] = his opinion or forecast · [HYPOTHESIS] = our testable version.

**Transcript caveats** (auto-captions): "Jeffre" = Jefferies; "Highex/Highinex" = SK Hynix; "DF" = most likely **DLF**; "LODA" = **Lodha** (Lodha Developers); "Bajash Finance" = Bajaj Finance; "Kevin Walsh" = most likely Kevin Warsh; "Corey" = most likely CoreWeave. Numbers spoken in passing (gold levels, yields) may be mis-transcribed. Note also that the episode is broker-sponsored (Groww), and that Wood describes his own model portfolios.

## 3. Key learnings (frameworks, not forecasts)

1. **New-technology cycles:** impact is overestimated early and underestimated later. The AI analogy he prefers is 19th-century US railroads: the infrastructure got built and was useful, but its financiers went bust. [VIEW]
2. **EPS vs free cash flow divergence** is a late-cycle warning. Capex inflates reported EPS for suppliers while FCF falls for spenders. Depreciation schedules, off-balance-sheet data centres and circular (vendor-style) financing are accounting red flags. [VIEW]
3. **Financing shift = cycle stage:** cash-funded capex → debt-funded capex marks the later part of the cycle. [VIEW]
4. **Flows are benchmark-driven:** FII selling in India is largely *relative* — EM funds chasing Korea and Taiwan memory weights (TSMC + Samsung + SK Hynix ≈ 30% of the EM index) [FACT claim]. India is a "negative-AI" trade: an AI unwind brings foreigners back.
5. **The 10Y yield matters more than the Fed funds rate.** Long yields ≈ nominal GDP growth + a rising fiscal term premium. [VIEW/THEORY]
6. **Yield-curve-control transmission:** if bond yields are capped, weakness moves to the currency, which is bullish for gold. [VIEW, Japan precedent]
7. **Failed reaction to good news:** gold failing to make a new high on a major geopolitical shock signalled consolidation. [VIEW, testable]
8. **Product prices are better than crude for gauging oil damage:** diesel rose much more than crude. [VIEW, testable]
9. **Hedge a risk by owning its beneficiary:** energy stocks against an oil shock. [VIEW]
10. **Indian index is supply-constrained:** domestic MF/SIP inflows are absorbed almost one-for-one by equity supply (IPOs, QIPs, promoter and PE selling). This makes it a **bottom-up stock-picker's market** despite ~15% earnings growth. [VIEW, testable]
11. **Rate cycle and financials:** RBI hikes favour banks over NBFCs (funding-cost asymmetry). [THEORY, testable]
12. **Miners = leveraged gold, short energy:** margins depend on gold *minus* energy cost. [THEORY, testable]

## 4. Backtest candidates

None of these has been tested. Each is a [HYPOTHESIS].

| # | Hypothesis | Data needed | Method | Main risks / bias |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B1** | Gold-miner returns ≈ β₁·gold − β₂·oil; miners outperform gold when gold ↑ and oil ↓ | GDX, GLD/gold futures, WTI (2006+) | Rolling regression; regime split by oil trend | Equity beta confounder; GDX composition changes |
| **B2** | RBI hiking cycles → private banks outperform NBFCs over 6–12 months | Nifty Bank / Nifty Pvt Bank vs NBFC basket (Bajaj Fin, Shriram, Cholamandalam, etc.); RBI policy dates | Event study from first hike in each cycle | Only ~4–5 cycles since 2010 → descriptive, not statistical; survivorship in the NBFC basket |
| **B3** | Indian realty under-performs during RBI hiking cycles, then leads after the last hike | Nifty Realty, Nifty 50, repo history | Relative-return event study | Same small sample; property cycle confounds |
| **B4** | High net equity supply (IPOs + QIPs + OFS + block deals) relative to MF equity inflows predicts weaker forward Nifty returns | SEBI/AMFI monthly flows, primary-market data (e.g. Prime Database) | Monthly "net liquidity" indicator → 3–12 month forward index returns; also small-cap vs large-cap | Release lags (AMFI ~10th of next month) → point-in-time alignment; short history |
| **B5** | US 10Y > 4.5% / > 5% regimes predict weaker equity returns and stronger gold | FRED DGS10 (daily), S&P 500, Nifty (USD and INR), gold | Regime analysis on **changes/percentiles**, not fixed levels | Fixed thresholds chosen with hindsight; non-stationary rates (pre-2008 yields often above 5%) |
| **B6** | Gold failing to make a new N-day high within k days after a geopolitical-risk spike → lower 3-month forward return | Gold daily; Caldara–Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk (GPR) index (daily) | Conditional event study | Event definition is subjective; few large events |
| **B7** | Diesel-crude spread (crack) leads crude price / oil-importer equity performance | NYMEX HO/RBOB/CL or ICE gasoil vs Brent | Lead-lag regression | Fits the commodity program (crack spreads) |
| **B8** | **FCF-to-earnings conversion filter** improves momentum / CANSLIM selection (avoid high-EPS, low-FCF names) | Point-in-time fundamentals for the Indian/US universe | Add the filter to the existing screen; compare | Well-known accruals anomaly (Sloan 1996) — test for incremental value only; needs point-in-time data |
| **B9** | Hyperscaler stock reaction to capex-guidance raises is a regime signal for AI-supplier stocks | Earnings dates, capex guidance (manual), stock returns | Event study (~4 firms × ~12 quarters) | Very small N; manually collected data |
| **B10** | Bitcoin 4-year halving cycle | BTC prices | **Not testable statistically** (~4 cycles) | Descriptive only |

**Highest research value for you:** B8 (directly improves your equity screen), B4 (India-specific and novel), B1 (also feeds the commodity program), B2/B3 (simple, but small samples).

## 5. Implementation notes (for your equity process)

- **Use his themes as watchlists, not as buy signals.** Make entries conditional on your trend template, breakout or VCP rules.
  - He explicitly says Indian property is "out of favour short term". Your trend filter should decide timing.
- **Watchlist themes:**
  1. Indian real estate: DLF, Lodha and peers.
  2. Private banks.
  3. Gold-loan financiers (Muthoot Finance, Manappuram are *theme examples*; he did not name them).
  4. Bajaj Finance.
  5. Eternal (Zomato).
  6. Power / renewables / storage.
  7. Gold (MCX gold, gold ETFs).
  8. Energy (as a hedge sleeve).
- **Risk overlays to test before using:**
  - US 10Y breaching 5% as a risk-off flag (B5).
  - Middle East escalation → reduce mid/small-cap exposure (his view; untested).
- **Avoid list per his view:** Indian IT services. This conflicts with momentum only if IT is trending up — let price decide.
- **Conflict checks:**
  - He is a 3-year strategist; your process is momentum/swing. His horizon does not equal yours.
  - Model-portfolio weights (5%, 20% gold) are for diversified institutional portfolios, not position-sizing advice.
